WebRoot/auth/admin/addER.jsp: As an administrator using this healthcare system, you are responsible for adding new Emergency Responders. To achieve this, you need to input the Emergency Responder's first name, last name, and email address into the designated fields of the form. Once you submit this form, the system creates a new Emergency Responder account, assigning a unique Medical ID (MID) and generating a temporary password for the new personnel. You will receive a confirmation message displaying the Emergency Responder’s MID and temporary password, which you need to communicate to the new responder. You will then have the option to continue to another page to further manage or edit personnel information. This process ensures that new responders are added efficiently and securely while you provide them with the necessary credentials to access the system.

WebRoot/auth/admin/addHCP.jsp: As a healthcare administrator using this system, you would start by entering details such as the first name, last name, and email address of the new healthcare professional (HCP) into the provided form. After submitting the form, the system creates a new HCP record, assigning a unique Medical ID (MID) to them. A temporary password is also generated, which you should pass on to the HCP to allow them to log in and change it later. You’ll receive a confirmation with the assigned MID and the temporary password. You can then proceed to manage the newly added personnel's information, ensuring that all necessary credentials and details are securely managed and communicated. This streamlined process helps integrate new healthcare workers into the system efficiently, while safeguarding sensitive information.

WebRoot/auth/admin/addPHA.jsp:
As an administrator utilizing this system, you would:  
Fill out the form with the personnel's first name, last name, and email address when adding a new Public Health Authority (PHA).  
Submit the information, and the system will automatically create a new personnel profile and assign a unique identifier, known as a Medical ID (MID), to the individual.  
The system will generate a temporary password for the newly added personnel, which you can ensure reaches them for accessing their account securely.  
After the addition, a confirmation message will display the MID and temporary password of the new PHA. You can then proceed to manage or edit their personnel details further on another page.  
This process is streamlined to ensure accuracy in personnel management and immediately enable account creation for Public Health Authorities within the organization.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editApptType.jsp: As an administrator using this system, you can manage and maintain the list of appointment types offered within your organization. You have the ability to add new appointment types or update existing ones. You’d start by entering the name and duration for the appointment type you wish to add or update in the respective fields. Submit the form using the appropriate button for your action: either "Add Type" to create a new appointment type or "Update Type" to modify an existing one. If validation errors occur, such as missing information, the system will alert you to correct it. Additionally, you can view a list of current appointment types along with their durations. By clicking on an appointment type's name in the list, you can quickly autofill the form to update the appointment type's details. This setup facilitates efficient management of the services provided to clients by allowing you to keep appointment types up-to-date easily.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editCPTProcedureCodes:
As an administrator using this system, you can manage CPT procedure codes, which are standardized medical procedure identifiers. Here's how you interact with the system: 

1. You can add a new CPT procedure code by providing a unique code, a description of the procedure, and indicating whether it is related to immunization. Once you input this information into the form and click "Add Code," the system will process the details, validate the input, and add the procedure to the code list if all criteria are met.

2. You can update an existing CPT procedure code by selecting it from the current list. When you click on a listed code, the form automatically populates with its existing details (code and description). You can update the description or change the immunization status. After making updates, clicking "Update Code" will modify the procedure details.

3. The system displays all active CPT codes in a table, showing their code, description, and whether they pertain to immunizations. You can view details of a code by clicking on its description.

4. If any input you provide fails validation or encounters issues, the system will display an error message at the top of the page, guiding you to resolve the problem.

This process simplifies the management of procedure codes, supporting accurate updates and additions while ensuring compliance with data integrity rules.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editICDCodes.jsp: As an administrator maintaining medical records within a healthcare system, you can manage the list of International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes by adding new codes or updating existing ones. Start by viewing the current ICD codes displayed in a table. If you need to update a code, click on the description, which will populate the form with the existing details of that code, allowing you to make necessary changes. You can specify if the condition is chronic by checking the appropriate box. For adding a new code, enter the code and description in the provided fields and indicate if it is chronic. Submit the form to either add a new code or update an existing one. You will receive a confirmation message regarding the success or failure of the operation, ensuring the integrity and accuracy of diagnostic information within the medical records. This streamlined process enhances the efficiency of managing diagnostic codes, contributing to better organizational and healthcare outcomes.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editLOINCCodes.jsp:
As an administrator using this system, you would:
Review the current list of codes, each representing a specific lab procedure.
To add a new code, fill out the form with relevant details such as the code, component, kind of property, time aspect, system, scale type, and method type. Each field needs to have appropriate valid information.
To update an existing code, click on the specific field in the list, and the system will fill the form with the existing information. Modify any fields that need updating while ensuring unchanged details remain accurate.
Submit the form using the 'Add Code' button to add a new code or the 'Update Code' button to update existing information.
Based on your actions, the system will provide a confirmation or error message, helping you ensure that codes are added or updated correctly within the lab procedures list. This functionality helps maintain precise and up-to-date lab procedure information crucial for managing medical records.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editNDCInteractions.j: As an administrator using this system, you can manage drug interactions by following these steps: Begin by selecting two medications from the provided lists, which display the available National Drug Codes (NDC) alongside their descriptions. Next, input a clear description of the interaction in the provided text field. Once you've added all required information, submit the form to register a new drug interaction in the system. If successful, you will see a confirmation, otherwise errors will be displayed for issues such as invalid inputs. It's important to provide accurate drug interaction details, as this information can significantly impact patient care and safety in healthcare settings.

WebRoot/auth/admin/editNDCodes.jsp: As an administrator using this system to manage National Drug Codes, you can perform several key functions related to medication code maintenance. You can add new medication codes by entering a specific code and description into the form provided. If there are updates to existing medication details, you can modify these by selecting the code from a list, making necessary changes, and submitting the updated information. The system also allows deletion of any drug interaction records, ensuring the details remain current and accurate. For viewing the list of existing codes, the system presents a structured list where each entry can be expanded to show interactions with other drugs. This interface thus supports the administrative task of maintaining an accurate and compliant drug database efficiently.

WebRoot/auth/admin/home.jsp: As a system administrator accessing the dashboard, you would be greeted with a personalized welcome message displaying your username. The interface appears to provide a simple entry-point for further navigation or administrative actions, while offering a welcoming user experience aimed at acknowledging your presence on the system. There are no additional administrative functions or data management tasks explicitly detailed on this introductory page.

WebRoot/auth/admin/hospitalAssignments.j: As an administrator using this system, you can manage staffing assignments for healthcare providers (HCPs) to various hospitals. To begin, make sure a valid personnel ID is in the system. If it's missing, you'll be redirected to enter it. Once the ID is confirmed, you'll see a list of hospital assignments associated with the provider, along with a separate list of available hospitals. You can easily move the provider between hospitals by clicking "Assign" for assigning them to a new hospital or "Unassign" to remove their assignment. This ensures that healthcare providers are allocated properly across facilities, helping to maintain adequate staffing levels and facilitate efficient healthcare management.

WebRoot/auth/admin/hospitalListing.jsp: As an administrator using this system, you are able to manage hospital information efficiently. You can add new hospitals by providing a unique hospital ID and hospital name in the input fields, then selecting the option to add the hospital. If you need to update existing hospital details, you select the hospital name from the displayed list, which automatically fills the form with the current data, and edit the information before submitting the changes. The system will show a confirmation message reflecting whether the addition or update was successful, or if any validation errors occurred. This functionality ensures that you can maintain up-to-date and accurate records of all hospitals associated with your organization.

WebRoot/auth/admin/information.jsp: As an administrator using the system, you can access your personal information on this page. Upon visiting, the page displays your profile picture along with your full name as stored in the system. Currently, the location field is static and shows a default message. This page is meant to provide a quick view of your essential information, such as your name and your picture associated with your user ID, ensuring you are viewing the correct profile. There are no functionalities for editing information on this page; it primarily serves as a personal informational overview.

WebRoot/auth/admin/menu.jsp: As an administrator utilizing this system, you have several key functionalities at your disposal. Firstly, you can add new entities such as healthcare providers, emergency responders, or public health authorities to the system. For editing-related tasks, you can modify appointment types, manage hospital assignments for healthcare providers, and update various medical code standards including CPT, ND, ICD, and LOINC codes. Furthermore, you have the ability to edit personnel information and update your personal demographic details. In terms of system reminders, you can send appointment reminders and check the reminder message outbox to maintain effective communication with patients. Additionally, you can manage and update hospital listings, adjust global session timeout settings for user sessions, and review patient satisfaction survey results to gauge feedback and improve service delivery. These functions collectively allow you to manage operational aspects, optimize resource allocation, and ensure quality healthcare services within your organization.

WebRoot/auth/admin/remindersMessageOutbo: As an administrator using this system, you would access your Reminders Message Outbox to view sent reminder messages. You can sort these messages either by the recipient's name or the time they were sent. When you arrive at this function, a list of all your sent reminder messages will be displayed, and you can apply sorting options to facilitate easier access to specific messages. If you have chosen to sort by name, your messages will be ordered alphabetically based on the recipient's name. If you choose to sort by time, the messages will be ordered according to when they were sent. Additionally, you will have the opportunity to order them in either ascending or descending order according to your preference. From the displayed list, you can see details such as whom the message was sent to, the subject of the message, and the date it was sent. You can choose to view the content of any specific message by selecting the read option associated with it. If there are no messages present, an indication that there are no messages available is displayed. This function helps streamline the management of communication with recipients by offering an organized view of all outgoing reminder messages.

WebRoot/auth/admin/sendAppointmentRemind:
As an administrator using this system, you can automate the process of sending appointment reminders to patients. Here's how you achieve this:

1. Start by entering the number of days before an appointment when you want to send the reminders into the provided "threshold" field.
2. Submit the form to initiate the reminder sending process.
3. The system will identify all upcoming appointments that fall within the specified threshold and send reminder messages to the respective patients.
4. Each message will include details such as the appointment date and time, doctor’s name, and the number of days remaining until the appointment.
5. After the process is complete, you'll see a confirmation indicating the number of reminder messages successfully sent.
6. If an error occurs, such as entering an invalid value for the threshold, the system will display a relevant error message to guide you.

This feature helps ensure patients are reliably informed about their upcoming appointments, enhancing scheduling efficiency and reducing missed appointments.

WebRoot/auth/admin/sessionTimeout.jsp:
As an administrator using this system, you would:

Specify the session timeout interval by entering the desired number of minutes into a form. This interval determines how long an account can remain inactive before needing to re-authenticate. The minimum timeout interval is 1 minute.

Submit the form to update the session timeout setting. Once the timeout is successfully changed, a confirmation message will inform you that changes will take effect upon the next authentication.

This allows you to customize and enforce security measures by controlling inactive session durations across user accounts.

WebRoot/auth/admin/viewAllReportRequests:
As an administrator using this system, you have the ability to manage requests for generating reports:

1. You are presented with a table listing all report requests. Each request includes details such as the request's ID, the patient associated with the report, the approver, dates (requested, approved, and viewed), the current status of the request, and any comments.

2. For report requests with a status indicating they are awaiting approval ("Requested"), you can:
   - Choose to approve the request by selecting the "Approve" option. Once approved, a confirmation message will appear indicating the request was successfully accepted.
   - Choose to reject the request by selecting the "Reject" option. After initiating a rejection, the system will prompt you to enter a reason for rejecting the request. Once you provide a comment and confirm the rejection, the request is marked as rejected.

3. If you make any operational errors or encounter issues (e.g., entering incorrect data), the system will display an error message to help you understand the problem.

This page facilitates the seamless management and oversight of report requests within the organization, ensuring that report approvals and rejections are handled efficiently and transparently.

WebRoot/auth/admin/viewReminderMessage.j:
As an administrator using this system, you would:

Open the "View Reminder Message" interface, where details of a specific message can be reviewed. Messages are typically reminders sent to other users.

When accessing the page, the system checks if a specific message has been selected through the message ID provided. If no message ID is found, or if there's an error in the input, you are redirected to the appropriate outbox or inbox page to make a valid selection.

Once a valid message is identified, the system retrieves and displays the following details:
- The recipient's name (using the message's subject to identify the recipient's ID and name).
- The subject of the message after removing any ID identifiers.
- The date and time when the message was initially sent.
- The full body content of the message.

The system also marks the message as "read," ensuring accurate tracking of message statuses.

This process provides you with a streamlined way to access, review, and manage reminder messages sent from your account while maintaining clarity in the communication workflow.

WebRoot/auth/admin/visitGraph.jsp: As an administrator utilizing this system, you can visualize patient visit trends over a specified period. Begin by selecting the start and end months and years from dropdown menus and generate a report. The system will then compute the number of visits for minors and adults within the selected period. If any errors occur, such as entering a start date that's after the end date or selecting future dates, the system will display an error message. Once the report runs successfully, a graph will display showing the number of visits over the chosen months, differentiated by minors and adults for easy comparison.

WebRoot/auth/er/home.jsp: As a user accessing this page, you can view announcements related to new features of the system, such as the addition of a calendar pop-up for easier date selection. This page also serves as a central area for notifications, though no specific notifications are displayed in this snippet. The system provides a streamlined way to stay informed about updates and changes, ensuring ease of use and improved interaction with key features.

WebRoot/auth/er/information.jsp: If you are an employee accessing this system, you would view your personal information on a dedicated page. Upon logging in, the system will display your name, city, and state on the page. Additionally, you'll see your picture associated with your user ID. This functionality allows you to verify and confirm your details easily within the workplace system without needing to access additional resources or databases.

WebRoot/auth/er/menu.jsp: As a user of this system, you can access an emergency patient report by clicking on the designated link provided in the menu. This function is categorized under "Report", making it easy to locate. The system likely provides critical information about patients that may be required during urgent or emergency situations. Through this straightforward interaction, you can retrieve essential data quickly for decision-making in emergency scenarios.

WebRoot/auth/exceptionHandler.jsp: When an error occurs during the use of the system, users are automatically redirected to a designated page. The system collects and stores information about the error, including its type and message, so it can be reviewed later. This provides a seamless experience by quickly redirecting the user to an appropriate resolution flow without requiring manual intervention or displaying technical details. Users can continue their tasks without being disrupted by technical jargon or application crashes.

WebRoot/auth/forwardUser.jsp: Upon successfully logging into the system, users are automatically checked for their roles and redirected to their respective home pages, which are personalized based on their role within the organization. These roles can include patient, healthcare provider, user access personnel, emergency responder, public health authority, administrator, or tester. Each user type is directed to an appropriate dashboard that contains specific information and functions related to their role. However, if a valid session is not detected or the user's credentials are not recognized by the system, they are logged out or redirected to an error page informing them that they do not have access to proceed further. This security mechanism ensures that users only access information and functionalities pertinent to their responsibilities.

WebRoot/auth/getPatientID.jsp: As a user of this system, you will be able to search for and select a specific patient record by utilizing a convenient search functionality based on the patient's first and last name. Firstly, greet the interface designed to facilitate your need to access patient information. You can either directly input the patient's unique ID if known, or use a search form to specify the first and last name of the patient you wish to find. After entering the search criteria, initiate the search to receive a list of matching patients. From the results, you can easily select the desired patient by clicking on their identification button, which will then proceed to another page with further details. This user-friendly system ensures quick access to patient records, allowing for streamlined workflow and efficient patient data handling.

WebRoot/auth/getPersonnelID.jsp: As a user, you would engage with the system to find and select a specific personnel's information. You can search for personnel by entering their first and last names. Upon conducting a search, the system will display a list of personnel that match the provided criteria. Each entry in the list will have a button you can click, which selects the respective personnel. Once you select a personnel, the system forwards you to the appropriate resource based on the context you defined. This process assists you in quickly identifying and selecting relevant personnel by matching their names, facilitating efficient user identification and selection.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/addUAP.jsp:
As a healthcare provider adding administrative personnel (UAP) to the system, you would:

Enter the first name, last name, and email address of the new staff member into the provided form. If an email address is unavailable, you can use a pre-defined hospital email for password recovery purposes.

Once you submit the form, the system will create a new record for the staff member. It will assign them a unique Medical ID (MID), generate a temporary password, and classify their role as a UAP.

Afterward, the system will display a confirmation message with the staff’s MID and temporary password. You can pass this information securely to the newly added personnel to allow them access to the system.

Following the successful addition, you would have the option to navigate to another page to further manage or edit the personnel's information.

This process streamlines the addition of UAP staff members and ensures all essential information for their onboarding is created securely and available immediately.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/calendar.jsp: As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you can manage and view calendar-based appointments seamlessly. The system allows you to browse through the calendar, viewing appointments scheduled for each specific day within a month. You can navigate between different months using the 'Last' and 'Next' links, helping you to plan ahead or revisit past appointments. Each day will display the number of appointments along with a link to view detailed information about each one. Colored markings may indicate appointment conflicts, enabling you to quickly identify and resolve scheduling issues.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/editPatientList.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system, you start by ensuring you have selected a patient using their Medical ID (MID). If not, the system redirects you to a page where you can enter this ID. Once a patient is selected, you can either add or remove them from your monitoring list. Upon submitting your choice, the system confirms whether the patient was successfully added or removed from the list with a message displaying the patient's status change. You also have the option to choose a different patient for editing by clicking a button, which resets the selection, allowing you to start the process with a new MID. This functionality helps in efficiently managing patients under your care by keeping track of those who need regular monitoring.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/editRepresentatives.jsp: As a healthcare provider managing patient representatives, you would start by retrieving the Patient ID for whom you want to edit representative information. If the ID is not already specified, the system will prompt you to locate the patient ID first. Once you have selected a patient, you may add representatives or remove existing ones. Representatives are responsible for managing certain aspects of the patient’s healthcare information. After making changes, you will receive a confirmation message about the success of your actions. This system enables you to efficiently manage relationships between patients and their representatives, ensuring that the correct individuals have access to the necessary information to assist patients in their care. The list of current representatives is displayed, allowing you to view and manage them with ease, ensuring proper communication and representation arrangements.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/hcpConsultation.jsp:
As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you would:

1. Navigate to the HCP Consultations page to manage your consultations.
2. To send a consultation, select the 'Send a Consultation' option:
   - Choose a patient from your list of associated patients.
   - Choose another HCP to refer the patient to.
   - Provide details about the referral, and submit the form.
   - The system will send the consultation request, and you will receive a confirmation of submission.
3. To view pending consultations, select the 'View Pending Consultations' option:
   - You will see two lists of consultations: outgoing and incoming.
   - You can view the current status (Pending, Finished, or Declined) of each referral, the patient's information, the sender's and receiver's details.
   - You can update a pending consultation referral by clicking the 'edit' option.
4. When updating a consultation:
   - Review and if needed, update the referral and consultation details based on whether you are the sending or receiving HCP.
   - You can change the status of the referral.
   - Submit the updated form to finalize the update and receive a confirmation of the changes made.
5. Manage consultation details, ensuring clear and accurate information is shared while maintaining the confidentiality and proper patient management protocols.

This system allows efficient and secure communication among healthcare providers regarding patient referrals, facilitating better coordination and patient care.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/home.jsp:
As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you would:

1. Start on the home page where you can view important announcements regarding new features in the system, such as the introduction of a calendar tool for easier date entry.
2. Review your notifications, which include:
   - Comprehensive report history: If you have any pending report requests, you can see updates and the current status of each report. If no report requests are available, the system will inform you.
   - A list of lab procedures completed in the last month: You can see details of lab procedures tied to specific patients. For each procedure, you’ll see the patient's name, relevant lab procedure codes, and any recorded results. In cases where results are not yet available, you’ll be notified accordingly.
3. Access a link to view all lab procedures in greater detail, enabling you to manage or follow up on laboratory workflows.
   
Overall, this system allows you to conveniently track your ongoing tasks and recently completed procedures while keeping you informed about updates and changes relevant to your operations. This creates an efficient workflow tailored to typical healthcare provider responsibilities.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/information.jsp: As a user of the system, you can view your personal information, including your profile picture and basic details such as name and location. Upon accessing this page, the system will automatically retrieve and display the information relevant to your user ID. This allows you to quickly confirm and verify your profile details in a concise and organized layout. If any information appears incorrect, you may need to take action through another part of the system to update or correct your data.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/LabProcHCP.jsp:
As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you can:

- View the laboratory procedures associated with your patients, categorized by patient name, lab code, rights, status, commentary, results, and related office visit details. This allows you to track and assess the progress of lab procedures and their outcomes.
- Modify access rights to specific laboratory procedures, determining whether they are viewable by others depending on the privacy settings.
- Update the information on individual lab procedures when necessary, ensuring that the records are accurate and reflect the latest details.
- Navigate to the office visit record that is connected to a lab procedure, allowing further edits or updates to the visit's details.
- Manage cases where no laboratory procedures are registered for a patient, which will be displayed with a “No Data” message for easier identification.

This facilitates comprehensive management of laboratory procedures for patients in a structured and accessible manner while addressing privacy concerns through user-adjustable settings.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/menu.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system, you have access to a comprehensive dashboard that organizes your functions into clear categories. You can quickly add new patients or users who require access to the system. Editing options allow you to update basic health information, manage demographic details, and alter patient and representative data. Scheduling and reviewing appointments are streamlined under the appointments section, ensuring you maintain an organized calendar. Messaging capabilities help manage your inbox and outbox seamlessly. The view section offers insights into patient visit histories, your appointment schedule, laboratory procedures, and any report requests you’ve made. Emergency report generation and telemedicine tools help you provide urgent care and manage remote patient monitoring. Additional functions like documenting office visits, consulting, and reviewing chronic disease risks ensure you deliver holistic care while staying informed about patient communication and satisfaction trends. This intuitive layout optimizes your workflow, allowing efficient management of your healthcare responsibilities.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/messageInbox.jsp: As a healthcare professional accessing this system, you can efficiently manage and organize your messages. Upon accessing your message inbox, you have the option to sort your messages either by the sender's name or by the time they were received, and you can choose whether to display them in ascending or descending order. You can filter messages based on specific criteria such as the sender, subject, keywords that should or should not be present, and a date range. This filter can be tested before being saved, allowing for customization in viewing important communication. Messages appear in a list format where unread messages are highlighted for easy identification. You can select any message to read its contents. If no messages are available, you'll be informed accordingly. This system streamlines message handling, ensuring effective communication management in your professional environment.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/messageOutbox.jsp:
As a healthcare provider using this system, you would:

Access your personal message outbox to review all messages you have sent. The system displays the messages clearly, including details such as the recipient's name, the subject of the message, and the date it was sent.

If you have sent many messages, you can sort and organize them either by the recipient's name or the time the message was sent. When sorting, you can choose to display the messages in either ascending or descending order for better clarity and navigation.

For each message, there is an option to read its full content, providing an easy way to revisit and review any message you have dispatched.

If the outbox is empty, the system will display a message indicating that no messages are available.

Additionally, you’ll have a convenient link to compose a new message directly from the outbox, allowing seamless transitions between reviewing your communications and initiating new ones.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/monitorPatients.jsp:
As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you would:
Check the list of patients being monitored for vital signs and other health data.
The list will show each patient's name along with their medical ID, the date the data was recorded, and specific metrics such as systolic and diastolic blood pressure and glucose levels.
Some rows may be highlighted if the data is out of a predefined safe range, which could indicate potential health issues requiring attention.
You can click on a patient's name to view more detailed information about that patient's health data.
This system helps in identifying patients who may need closer observation or immediate intervention.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/reply.jsp: As a healthcare provider, this system allows you to respond to messages received from patients or other colleagues. When replying to a message, you'll view the original sender's details and be prompted to enter a response. You can input a subject line, which will be pre-populated with the original subject prefaced by "RE:", and compose your message in the provided text area. Once you submit your reply, the message will be sent back to the original sender, and you'll be redirected to your message inbox, ensuring efficient communication within the healthcare setting.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/scheduleAppt.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system, you would navigate to the page to schedule an appointment for a patient. First, ensure that you have selected the correct patient. If not, the system will direct you to a page to confirm or select the correct patient ID. Once the patient is confirmed, you will choose the type of appointment from a list that includes duration details. You will need to select a date and time for the appointment using the available fields for scheduled date, hour, and minutes, as well as specifying AM or PM. Optionally, you can include comments regarding the appointment for personalized notes. After filling out the form correctly, you can submit the appointment request. If everything is appropriately entered, a success message will confirm the scheduling, and you will be redirected to the home page to continue your workflow. If there's an error, such as an unfilled date, appropriate messages will guide you to correct the errors. This process allows you to efficiently handle patient appointments within your practice's scheduling system.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/sendEmailNotification.j: As a healthcare provider, you use this system to send email notifications to patients. If you intend to send an email, you first select the patient by entering their Medical ID (MID). If there's a match, a form opens where you can view your own name in the sender's field and the patient's email and full name in the recipient's field. You determine the purpose of the email by filling out the subject and message body, which already starts with a polite salutation using the patient’s first name. Upon submission, the email is sent to the patient. You'll then see a confirmation displaying the email details and can choose to go back to your main portal page. This process allows you to communicate important reminders or notifications to patients efficiently, ensuring accurate delivery using their registered email information.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/sendMessage.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system, you can send messages to patients securely. First, ensure that the patient's ID is retrieved for whom you want to send the message. You will be redirected to identify the patient if the ID is not available. Once the patient is identified, you can type the subject and the message body into the designated fields. Upon submission, the message will be sent to the selected patient. The system will notify you of any errors if the information provided is incomplete or incorrect. After sending, the system directs you to the message outbox to manage your messages. This process facilitates easy and quick communication with patients directly within the healthcare management system.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/UpdateLabProc.jsp: As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you can update a patient's lab procedure information. To do so, you would retrieve the lab procedure details using the patient ID, then update key information such as the status of the lab procedure (e.g., not yet received, pending, completed), the results, and any commentary or notes related to the procedure. After submitting your updates, the system will process and save the new information, confirming a successful update. This ensures that all lab procedures are accurately recorded and accessible for future reference, maintaining accurate medical records for patient care continuity. You can navigate to view all laboratory procedures once the updates are complete.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/viewAdditionalInfo.jsp: In this system aimed at remote healthcare monitoring, as a healthcare provider, you will be able to: Access detailed patient information based on remote monitoring data, which includes patient details like name and phone number. Additionally, you can identify patient representatives who act on behalf of the patient, providing any contact information they may have. You can view historical health statistics related to blood pressure and glucose levels for the patient. You can specify a date range to retrieve these monitoring statistics, offering you trend insights across specified timeframes. For health statistics that fall outside typical ranges, visual highlights provide immediate alerting, helping you gauge patient health at a glance. All information is accessible based on the patient's unique identifier from remote monitoring records, ensuring targeted and individualized data access for enhancing patient care delivery.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/viewAppt.jsp: As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you can view details of a specific appointment. When you select an appointment from your list of appointments, the system will display the patient's name, the type of appointment, the date and time it is scheduled, and the duration of the appointment in minutes. Additionally, any comments associated with the appointment will be displayed. If no comments are present, it will indicate so. This helps you quickly review essential details about the appointments you've scheduled.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/viewMessageInbox.jsp: As a healthcare professional accessing this system, you can view your message inbox to manage communications related to your healthcare practice. Upon logging in, you can see the messages that have been sent to you. If you have selected a specific message, the system will retrieve and display details about who sent it, the subject, the date and time it was sent, and the body of the message. You also have the option to reply to the message directly. The system ensures that you can view messages easily, providing vital communication features to maintain effective management of patient and colleague interactions within the healthcare environment. Any issues with viewing or accessing messages will redirect you to a safe page to prevent errors.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/viewMessageOutbox.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system, you can view the details of messages you have sent from your outbox. When navigating to this page, the system will display the recipient's name, the subject of the message, the date and time the message was sent, and the body of the message. This allows you to review and confirm the content of your communications with other users. If there was an error or invalid action, you will be redirected back to the outbox or another appropriate page to ensure proper navigation. After reviewing the message, you can click a provided link to return to the outbox for further message management. This process aids in efficient tracking and organization of sent communications while maintaining secure handling of message data.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/viewMyAppts.jsp:
As a healthcare provider utilizing this system, you can view a list of your scheduled appointments efficiently. Here's how the appointment management process works for you:

1. When accessing the page, you will see a table listing your upcoming appointments, including the patient's name, the type of appointment, the scheduled date and time, and the expected duration.

2. The system highlights any scheduling conflicts between appointments, allowing you to identify and resolve overlapping bookings.

3. For each appointment, you can review comments associated with it. If there’s a comment available, you can click on the "Read Comment" link to view detailed notes.

4. If there are no appointments scheduled for you, the system will display a message indicating the absence of any upcoming appointments.

This process enables you to manage your schedule and resolve potential conflicts, ensuring you can focus on delivering healthcare services effectively. You’re provided with clear insights into appointment details, such as duration and comments, but have the flexibility to navigate and manage your calendar seamlessly.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/viewMyMessages.jsp: As a healthcare provider (HCP), to view your messages, you would log into the system and access the page for viewing messages. This page is designed to display all the messages sent to you. If you have any messages, you will see them listed in a table format with details including the sender's name, the content of the message, and the date the message was received. There will also be an option to reply to a message directly by clicking the reply link next to each message. If there are no messages, the page will inform you that there are no messages in your inbox. This streamlined process ensures you can efficiently manage and respond to communications relevant to your medical practice.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/viewPrescriptionRenewal: As a healthcare provider accessing this system, you can view a list of your patients who have prescription renewal needs. Upon logging in, you will be presented with a table listing patients along with their contact details such as phone number and email address. If there are no patients needing prescription renewals, a message will display indicating no current needs. Each patient's name is clickable, allowing you to directly send an email notification regarding their prescription renewal. This facilitates timely communication and efficient management of patient prescription renewals.

WebRoot/auth/hcp/visitReminders.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system, you would interact with the visit reminder functionality by selecting a type of reminder from a dropdown list, which could include categories such as overdue check-ups or upcoming vaccinations. Upon submitting your selection, you would receive a list of patients who require visits based on the reminder type, including their contact information and reasons why a visit is flagged. You have the option to send email notifications directly to the patients by clicking on their names, facilitating communication and appointment scheduling. This feature aims to improve patient follow-up and ensure necessary medical visits occur as intended.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-er/emergencyReport.jsp: As a healthcare provider accessing this system's emergency report functionality, you will be able to generate a comprehensive report of a patient's crucial medical information. This includes the patient's name, age, gender, emergency contact, allergies, blood type, critical diagnoses, prescriptions, and immunizations. You begin by ensuring you have the correct Patient ID which the system verifies before generating the report. Upon verification, it notifies other healthcare providers associated with the patient about the report access through automated email notifications, maintaining transparency. For convenience, you have the option to generate a printable version of the report for offline review or sharing with other authorized professionals. This seamless integration and immediate availability of critical data enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of healthcare delivery, especially in urgent scenarios.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/addPatient.jsp:
As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you would:

Start by filling out a brief form to provide the new patient's first name, last name, and email address. If the patient doesn't have an email address, you can use the hospital's assigned email address to ensure they can recover their password later.

Submit the form to let the system process the patient registration. Once the process is completed, the system will create a unique Medical ID (MID) for the patient and generate a temporary password.

After successful registration, you will receive on-screen confirmation displaying the new patient's MID and temporary password. You are encouraged to securely forward this information to the patient so they can access their account.

You are then prompted to continue managing the patient's details and profile using a follow-up page for further actions, such as updating additional information or communicating specific instructions.

This workflow is designed to make the patient registration process straightforward while safeguarding sensitive information such as security questions and passwords. It ensures a secure and efficient way to onboard new patients into the system.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/chronicDiseaseRisks:
As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you would begin the process by ensuring you have selected a patient's medical ID (PID) either beforehand or through a prompt. Upon entering the PID, the system assesses the patient's health data to identify potential chronic diseases the patient may be at risk for. 

The system presents a list of chronic diseases along with associated risk factors specific to the selected patient. Each disease includes a detailed description of the individual patient risk factors contributing to the assessment. This provides a clear and organized view that helps you understand the patient's health profile and focus on preventive measures or targeted treatment.

If no data is available for the selected patient, the system informs you accordingly, allowing you to handle such instances with clarity. You would use this feature as part of preventative care planning or to monitor patients with ongoing health concerns.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/documentOfficeVisit:
As a healthcare professional using this system, you would:  
1. Select a patient, ensuring you have their unique identifier (PID) before proceeding. If the patient ID is not set, the system redirects you to first specify it.  
2. To document a new office visit for the patient, confirm your action through a single-click interface. After confirmation, the system will create a new office visit record and redirect you to a page where you can edit and input relevant visit details.  
3. Alternatively, you can view a list of past office visits for the patient and select any visit from the list to modify or update its details.  
4. This process streamlines the documentation of office visits, allowing you to focus on either creating new records or managing existing ones for accurate patient care history.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/editBasicHealth.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system, you would start by entering the system to edit a patient's basic health record. You can access a list of the patient's previous health records, displaying details such as height, weight, smoking status, blood pressure, cholesterol levels, and the date these details were last recorded, along with the recording personnel. If you need to add a new health record, click the button provided to display the input form. In this form, you'll fill out the patient's height, weight, their smoking status, blood pressure readings, and cholesterol measurements. Once completed, you submit the form to add the new record to the system. This process helps maintain accurate and up-to-date health information for patients, assisting in better health management and care delivery.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/editOfficeVisit.jsp:
Using this system as a healthcare provider, you would:

1. Start by identifying or selecting the patient and office visit record you want to document or update.
2. View and update basic visit details such as the date of the visit, hospital, and notes associated with the visit.
3. Add prescriptions for the patient by specifying medication details such as dosage, start and end dates, and instructions. The system checks for possible interactions and allergy warnings before confirming the prescription. You can also view or modify previous prescriptions tied to the visit.
4. Manage laboratory procedures by documenting or removing existing procedures and adding new ones using predefined LOINC codes. This includes setting statuses and commentary for these procedures.
5. Review and update patient diagnoses associated with this visit using ICD codes. You can add diagnoses from a provided list or remove existing ones if needed.
6. Document procedures performed during the visit by using CPT codes. You can add procedures to the visit record, and edit or remove past procedures.
7. Record immunizations administered during this office visit using specialized CPT codes, as well as add or remove immunization entries.
8. Confirm that updates are successfully saved or address potential issues flagged by the system (e.g., invalid inputs, drug interactions, allergies).
9. Navigate to other parts of the patient's record, such as personal health records or other historical data, once the office visit documentation is complete.

This workflow allows providers to efficiently document and make adjustments to office visit records, enabling accurate and thorough patient care management.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/editPatient.jsp:
As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you will:

1. Start by accessing the patient’s profile that you wish to edit. If you don't already have the patient's identifier, the system will guide you to enter the patient's ID.
2. Once you have access to the patient's profile, you can update various details including:
   - Personal Information: Modify fields such as the patient's first name, last name, email, physical address, phone number, and parental medical IDs.
   - Financial Data: Adjust the credit card type and number associated with the patient.
   - Insurance Information: Update the insurance provider's details including name, address, phone number, and insurance ID.
   - Emergency Contact: Update the emergency contact's name and phone number.
   - Health Information: You can modify the patient's ethnicity, blood type, gender, date of birth, date of death (if applicable), cause of death, and any relevant topical notes.
3. After entering the necessary information, submit the form to update the patient’s records. If the update is successful, you will see a confirmation message stating "Information Successfully Updated."
4. Note that you must use the "Reset Password" feature available on the login page if you need to set a new password for the patient.

This process ensures that patient information remains current and comprehensive, which is crucial for providing effective healthcare services.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/editPatientList.jsp: As a healthcare provider (HCP) using this system, you can manage your list of monitored patients through the following steps: First, ensure you have a specific patient's identification. The system will prompt you to select a patient if it doesn't detect one. Once you have the patient's identification, you'll be able to view their name and determine if they are already on your monitored list. You can then choose to either add them to or remove them from your list. Confirm your action, and the system will update your list accordingly. Afterward, the patient will be added or removed, confirmed through a message, and you will no longer need to select a patient for this interaction again until necessary.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/editPHR.jsp:
As a healthcare provider, you would use this system to manage and update comprehensive details of a patient's personal health record. 

You can begin by retrieving the patient's profile and confirming their identity. Once on the patient's page, you can:
- Review and verify the patient's general information, such as name, address, phone number, and email.
- Access and update the patient's insurance details, including provider name, address, and contact information.
- View or modify the patient's most recent basic health records, including height, weight, smoking status, blood pressure, and cholesterol levels. For historical data, you can navigate to the patient's health record history.
- Explore the patient's medical visit history and view details of previous office visits. Links are provided for accessing and editing individual office visits.
- Generate a prescription report for the patient if needed.

For the patient's family medical history, you can:
- View any recorded family members and their medical conditions such as high blood pressure, diabetes, and other chronic diseases.
- Link to or switch to a family member's records for more details.

In managing allergies:
- View a list of known allergies and their original discovery dates.
- Add new allergies directly through a form on the page.

To assess potential health risks:
- Use the tool provided to evaluate the patient's risk factors for chronic diseases. A detailed list of risks and links for further information are made visible upon request.

For immunizations:
- Inspect a record of immunizations the patient has received, with information such as the procedure code, description, and date received. Links are available for editing any related office visit containing immunization details.

This system is designed to offer a centralized repository for all key aspects of a patient's health records, streamlining management and ensuring all information is up to date and easily accessible.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/editPrescription.js: As a healthcare provider using this system, you can view and edit prescription information for your patients during their office visits. If you need to update a patient's prescription, you first select the office visit and prescription you wish to edit. Then, you will be presented with a form where you can modify the dosage and instructions for the medication. After entering the new information, you submit the form to save the changes, and the system confirms the update with a display of the revised prescription details. This process allows you to efficiently ensure that your patients receive accurate and current medication instructions based on their health needs. If any errors occur during the submission, the system will notify you, allowing you to attempt the update again, ensuring a smooth management of patient prescriptions.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/getPrescriptionRepo:
As a healthcare provider using this system, you can view a detailed prescription report for a specific patient. Here's how the process works: 

1. You start by selecting a patient using their unique Medical ID (MID). If the ID is not available, you will be redirected to another page to enter or confirm the patient's identity. 

2. Once the patient's information is confirmed, the system retrieves and displays their prescription records. These records include:
   - The national drug code (ND Code) of the medication.
   - A description of the medication.
   - The duration for which the medication is prescribed, including start and end dates.
   - The name of the healthcare provider who prescribed the medication.

3. If the selected patient does not have any prescription records, the system will inform you that no prescriptions are found.

4. All prescription details are presented in an easy-to-read table format for efficient review.  

This functionality helps ensure that you have accurate and organized access to patients' medication histories for better treatment and management decisions.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/LabProcUAP.jsp: As a healthcare provider using this system, you will be able to view laboratory procedures associated with a patient. First, you need to provide a patient ID. If you do not have an active patient ID, you will be directed to obtain one. Once you have the patient ID, you can view a list of laboratory procedures for that specific patient. This list includes details such as the patient's name, the lab code for the procedure, access rights, status of the lab procedure, any commentary or notes, results obtained, the associated office visit ID, and the last updated date. If you need to make any changes or updates to a lab procedure, you can click on the "Update" link next to the procedure, which will take you to a page where you can modify the details of that particular lab procedure. This streamlined process helps you efficiently manage and review laboratory data associated with your patients' healthcare records.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/showEmailHistory.js: As a healthcare professional (HCP) using this system, you would access the email history page to view correspondences previously sent. The page displays a list of all emails, including details such as recipient(s), subject, content, and the date each email was sent. If no emails are found in the records, the system will inform you that there are no emails on record. This functionality helps you keep track of email communications relevant to healthcare practices, ensuring transparency and easy reference for correspondence management.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/updateLabProc.jsp: As a healthcare provider user of this system, you access the functionality to update laboratory procedures. When you need to change the status, commentary, or results of a lab test, you retrieve the specific procedure using a unique identifier. The system displays the current details of the laboratory procedure, including patient ID, lab code, status, commentary, and results, among others. Upon making the necessary modifications, you submit the updated information through a form. If the updates are processed successfully, you receive a confirmation message. This process allows you to maintain up-to-date and accurate lab records, which is crucial for ensuring high-quality patient care and compliance with healthcare standards.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/viewMyReportRequest:
As a healthcare provider using this system, you can manage and review your report requests effectively. The page displays a list of all reports you have requested, providing key details such as the report ID, the patient's name, the requested date, the viewed date (if applicable), and the current status. You can click on an action link to view the details of a specific report.

If you need to add a new report request for a patient, you can do so by using the "Add a new Report Request" option. Once you add a request, the system processes it and includes it in your list of report requests. In cases where an error occurs during the submission of a new request, the system will notify you with a message.

This functionality ensures streamlined organization and easy access to patient-related reports within your workflow. It also encourages proactive engagement by allowing you to add and manage requests directly.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/viewPatientOfficeVi: As a healthcare provider utilizing this system, you can view a history of office visits for all patients. When accessing this feature, you will see a list of patients along with their addresses and the dates of their most recent visits. You have the opportunity to click on a patient's name to edit their personal health record information. This process allows you to efficiently track and manage patient office visit histories, helping ensure that all relevant information is up-to-date and easily accessible for patient care purposes.

WebRoot/auth/hcp-uap/viewReport.jsp:
This system allows healthcare providers to generate and view detailed comprehensive reports for their patients. As a provider, here's how you interact with the system:

You start by selecting a patient and a specific report request. Once selected, the system retrieves relevant details about the patient and organizes them into comprehensive categories.

The report includes the following:
1. **Personal Information**: Basic identification details like full name, address, phone number, and email.
2. **Insurance Details**: Information about the patient’s insurance carrier, payment information, and contact details.
3. **Health Records**: Data on various health metrics, including blood pressure, cholesterol levels, weight, height, and smoking status, along with the medical personnel responsible for recording these details.
4. **Diagnoses**: Details of any medical diagnoses the patient has received, categorized by visit ID, ICD code, and a description.
5. **Healthcare Providers**: A list of healthcare professionals designated for the patient.
6. **Allergies**: A summary of known patient allergies and their identification dates.
7. **Procedures**: Medical procedures performed on the patient, categorized by visit ID, codes, and descriptions.
8. **Prescriptions**: Details about medications prescribed, including the duration of the prescription, dosage, and instructions.
9. **Office Visits**: Records of the patient's medical visits, including dates, healthcare professionals, hospital IDs, and notes from the meeting.
10. **Family Connections**: A list of known family members along with the relationship type.
11. **Representation Links**: Information about other patients the current patient represents or is represented by.

This report serves as a centralized and easy-to-read document for overseeing patient history and current status comprehensively. It enables informed decision-making for monitoring health progress, identifying trends, and providing tailored care approaches. Providers can access this compiled data seamlessly to understand the patient's medical history and connections at a glance.

WebRoot/auth/patient/addTelemedicineData:
As a user (whether a patient or their representative) interacting with this system, you can report telemedicine data concerning blood pressure and glucose levels. Here's how:

- If you are self-reporting, simply enter your own readings for systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and glucose levels into the provided form and submit it.
- If you are reporting data for another patient (as their representative), select the specific patient from the provided list, which will automatically adjust the form to reference that individual. You then enter the readings for the selected patient and submit it.
- Upon submission, the system validates the entered data to ensure correct numerical formats. If any validation issues occur, an error message will be displayed, prompting you to correct your input.
- Once the data is successfully recorded, a confirmation message will appear to notify you of the successful addition of the information.

This process ensures accurate and secure reporting of key health metrics and allows for convenient reporting on behalf of others when necessary.

WebRoot/auth/patient/calendar.jsp:
As a patient using this system, you can view and manage your monthly schedule, including appointments, office visits, and lab procedures. The calendar displays days of the current month, highlighting the current day for easier navigation. You can use the "Last" and "Next" buttons to move between months.

For each day on the calendar:
- If you have scheduled appointments, office visits, or lab procedures, these will be listed under the respective dates. You’ll see a brief description of the event, such as the type of appointment, diagnosis, or lab details.
- Events marked as conflicts are clearly indicated to help prevent overlapping or problematic scheduling.

You can select "Read Details" next to any listed event to access more information, such as appointment specifics, visit details (including diagnoses or prescriptions), or lab procedure results. This empowers you to stay informed about your health-related activities and plan accordingly.

To update your personal information using this system, follow these steps:

1. Access the form that contains your current personal details. This form is designed to show the information the system already has recorded for you.
2. Update your basic information by entering your first name, last name, email, address (including street, city, state, and zip code), and phone number. This allows the system to keep your communication details current.
3. If you have parents recorded in the healthcare system, you can enter their identification numbers to link your records with theirs for familial medical history.
4. Update your payment information by selecting your credit card type and entering the card number. This ensures that your payment method is current for any necessary transactions.
5. Provide your insurance details by updating the insurer's name, address, phone number, and your personal insurance identification number. This keeps your coverage information accurate for billing and service purposes.
6. Enhance your account security by setting a security question and answer. This step helps in safeguarding your account and aids in account recovery.
7. Ensure your emergency contact is up-to-date by filling in their name and phone number. This information is crucial in case immediate family notification is required during medical situations.
8. Once all information has been reviewed and updated, submit the form to have the system store your changes. A confirmation message will acknowledge successful updates.
9. Remember, changing a password directly isn't possible through this form. Instead, use the reset password option available on the login page if necessary.

By following this process, you maintain your patient records' accuracy and security, ensuring the system supports your healthcare needs effectively.

WebRoot/auth/patient/home.jsp:
As a patient using this system, you are provided with an overview of your health-related activities, including lab procedures, survey completion, report history, and record access notifications. Within this interface, you can:

1. View personalized announcements and updates about system features.
2. Check for any unfinished surveys from your past office visits and complete them by following the provided links.
3. Access information about comprehensive report requests that you have made, including their current status.
4. Review a list of completed lab procedures from the last month and their associated results. For represented patients under your care, you can see a similar list of lab procedures completed recently.
5. Receive notifications about undesignated personnel accessing your medical records within the last 90 days to maintain awareness of privacy events.

Through this system, you can actively manage your health data, complete pending tasks like surveys, monitor lab results, and maintain an overview of access to your sensitive information. These functionalities are aimed to streamline health management and ensure data privacy.

WebRoot/auth/patient/information.jsp: As a patient accessing this system, you can view your personal information such as your name, gender, location (city and state), date of birth, and blood type. Additionally, a profile picture associated with your Medical ID (MID) will also be displayed. This view provides a summary of your details stored in the system, ensuring that you are informed about the recorded personal information.

WebRoot/auth/patient/menu.jsp:
As a patient using this system, you have a personalized menu that allows you to manage and access various aspects of your healthcare information and interactions. You can update your personal details under "My Demographics" or view logs of who accessed your records in "Access Log". Your medical history is accessible through sections like "My Diagnoses", "My Providers" for healthcare provider interactions, and "View My Records" for comprehensive access to your medical files. You can also review your current and expired prescription data.

Appointments are organized under "View My Appointments", letting you keep track of when and where you need to be for medical consultations. If you need to communicate with healthcare providers, the system offers a "Message Inbox" and "Message Outbox" for secure message exchanges. Telemedicine options are available for remote healthcare monitoring by reporting your health status.

For feedback and broader communication histories, you can review "Satisfaction Survey Results" and check "Show Email History" to revisit correspondence. This structured menu ensures a comprehensive, user-friendly experience tailored to managing your healthcare needs efficiently.

WebRoot/auth/patient/messageInbox.jsp:
As a patient using this system, you would:

- Access your message inbox to view communications sent to you. The messages may include sender details, subject, and the date received.  
- The system allows you to organize your messages by applying filters based on key criteria such as sender, subject, keywords, excluded words, or a date range. You can test or save these filters as needed.  
- You can sort your messages by sender name or time, and choose the order (ascending or descending).  
- Unread messages are highlighted for easy identification, ensuring you don't miss any important communications.  
- You have a link to read each message individually, which helps you access detailed information about each communication.  
- If there are currently no messages in your inbox, the system will inform you with a notification.  

This functionality provides a streamlined way for you to manage and view your messages effectively, with tools to filter, sort, and organize communications efficiently.

WebRoot/auth/patient/messageOutbox.jsp:
As a user viewing your sent messages, you would:  
1. Access your sent message outbox, which displays a list of previously sent messages.  
2. Optionally click on a "Compose a Message" link to create a new message if needed.  
3. Use sorting options provided to organize the list of sent messages based on:  
   - Recipient's name (in ascending or descending order).  
   - Time the message was sent (in ascending or descending order).  
4. Browse the sent messages, which show details such as the recipient's name, the subject of the message, and the date sent.  
5. Click on a "Read" link next to any message to view its content in detail.  
6. If there are no sent messages in your outbox, you'll simply see a message indicating that you have no messages.  

This process helps you effectively manage and monitor messages you’ve sent.

WebRoot/auth/patient/myDiagnoses.jsp:
As a patient using this system, you would:

View a list of your diagnoses, where each diagnosis is displayed with a description. You can click on any diagnosis to learn more about it.

Upon selecting a diagnosis, the system will provide detailed information about healthcare providers (HCPs) who have experience managing this specific condition. This includes their name, the number of patients they’ve treated, and related information like prescriptions they’ve issued, lab procedures they’ve ordered, and satisfaction ratings for both office visits and treatments.

Links are provided for further details about prescriptions or healthcare providers, enabling you to explore options and information easily.

If no HCPs have substantial experience with the selected diagnosis, the system will inform you that relevant data is unavailable.

This system helps you make informed decisions about your treatment options by offering personalized insights into diagnosis-specific expertise among healthcare providers.

WebRoot/auth/patient/reply.jsp:
As a patient using this system:  
You can reply to messages received from healthcare personnel. Initially, you select the message to reply to from your inbox. When replying, you'll see the details of the healthcare personnel who sent the original message, along with the subject line pre-filled as "RE: [Original Subject]."  
You can then write your reply in the provided text area and submit the response. After submission, the system creates a correspondence record linked to the original message and ensures the reply is securely delivered to the intended recipient. Upon successful submission, you are automatically redirected to your inbox to continue managing your messages.  
This feature allows for effective and direct communication within the healthcare environment, ensuring patients can interact smoothly with their care providers.

As a patient using this system, you can report any adverse reactions or issues experienced with prescribed medications by following these steps:

1. Navigate to the page for reporting an adverse event.
2. In the provided text area, describe the incident or reaction, providing as much detail as possible about the adverse event.
3. Submit your report through the "Save" button.

Upon submission:
- If you have multiple linked healthcare providers (HCPs), each HCP who prescribed medication involved in the event will receive a report. You can specify which provider to notify if applicable.
- The system will document the details of the adverse event, including the medication, prescribing provider, and your description.
- Notifications may be sent to healthcare providers to keep them informed and enable follow-up actions.

This process ensures that adverse events are recorded and communicated effectively to the relevant healthcare professionals, helping to address the issue and maintain patient safety.

WebRoot/auth/patient/sendMessage.jsp: As a patient using this system, you can send messages to your designated healthcare professionals or on behalf of another patient who has authorized you as a representative. To send a message, first, you will select the healthcare professional from a list of your declared healthcare providers. If you are sending on behalf of another patient, you will have the ability to choose from their healthcare providers as well. After selecting the appropriate recipient, you can enter the subject and content of the message. Once completed, submit the form to send the message. This process allows for secure communication between patients and healthcare providers, ensuring that messages are directed correctly and appropriately within the healthcare context.

WebRoot/auth/patient/showEmailHistory.js:
As a patient using this system, you can access a detailed history of all emails sent to you through the platform. When navigating to this section, you’ll see a table listing:

1. The recipients of each email.
2. The subject line of the email.
3. The body or main content of the email.
4. The date and time the email was sent.

If no email records exist, the system will display a message indicating that there are no emails on file. This function helps you keep track of communication and provides easy access to important correspondence related to your healthcare.

WebRoot/auth/patient/survey.jsp: As a patient using this system, you can provide feedback on your recent visit through a survey. To complete the survey, first indicate the amount of time you spent waiting in the waiting room and then the time spent in the examination room before seeing your doctor. Next, rate your satisfaction with the office visit overall, choosing from options ranging from very satisfied to very unhappy. Finally, rate your satisfaction with the treatment or information received, again selecting from similar options. After you've filled out the form, submit the survey. Upon successful submission, your feedback will be recorded and you’ll be redirected to your records page. This process allows you to easily report and assess your experiences during office visits.

WebRoot/auth/patient/viewAccessLog.jsp:
As a patient using this system to view your access log:  
You can filter the records based on a specific date range by entering the start and end dates into the provided fields and clicking the "Filter Records" button.  
The system will retrieve information about personnel or representatives who accessed your information during the specified date range.  

For each access entry, the system displays the date and time the access occurred, the name of the individual who accessed your information (with clickable links to view their details), their role (e.g., healthcare provider or personal health representative), and a brief description of the action taken, along with a code for the type of transaction.  
If no records are found for the selected filters, the table will display "No Data."  

If desired, you can sort records by either the date or the role of the individual by clicking on the respective column headers.  

This process helps you maintain visibility into who is accessing your personal healthcare information and supports transparency in record handling.
